messages:
Maya (CSE): Hey team, escalating a customer issue: they see duplicate token billing and sometimes duplicated partial generations after their client reconnects to our SSE stream. Repro steps attached.

Matt (customer): repro steps — 1) open SSE to /v1/streams with X-Client-Session: abc123 2) send prompt -> we get partial stream, connection drops after ~3s 3) client reconnects with same X-Client-Session and Resume-Id from last chunk, but server returns new generation and billing counts double. Happens ~3/5 runs.

Matt (customer): sample client side:```js
const es = new EventSource(url, {headers:{'Authorization': 'Bearer ...','X-Client-Session':'abc123'}});
es.onmessage = (e)=>{ /* append */ };
// onclose -> open new EventSource with same X-Client-Session + resume header
```

Maya (CSE): They also included server logs showing two completions around the disconnect window and a gap in seq numbers. Attaching snippets.

LogBot: [automated] logs ingest added to thread.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Thanks, Maya. First quick checks: are they using idempotency keys on the request body? Resume semantics should avoid re-generation if we see the same session + resume token. If the client reopens a fresh stream without the resume token we intentionally create a new generation.

Matt (customer): We're sending Resume-Id header. Example: `Resume-Id: r-0.3f2b` and `X-Client-Session: abc123`.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Ok. Can you paste the raw request/response headers from both connections around the failure? I want to confirm the resume token matched and that the first connection reported a committed final event (e.g., `event: committed`).

Matt (customer): pasted:```http
--> GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer redacted
X-Client-Session: abc123
Accept: text/event-stream

<-- 200 OK
event: partial
data: {"seq":1,"chunk":"foo"}

// connection drops

--> GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer redacted
X-Client-Session: abc123
Resume-Id: r-0.3f2b
Accept: text/event-stream

<-- 200 OK
event: partial
data: {"seq":1,"chunk":"foo"}
event: completion
data: {"id":"gen-842","tokens":45}
```

Alice (eng-oncall): Hmm: second stream starts at seq 1 again. That suggests server didn't persist the last ACKed seq for that session or the resume token wasn't associated with an in-progress generation. Could also be client reusing a token that expired server-side.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Two hypotheses: 1) Resume-Id accepted but the server started a new generation because the KV entry for session->generation was evicted (short TTL) 2) Resume token got assigned but a race caused a duplicate generation to start before resume reconciliation finished. Both could create double billing.

Elaine (CSE): Customer reports this started after they switched to our regional endpoint in EU-West. Could be routing to different regional runtime with slightly different state TTLs.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Good call. Regional routing can cause session state to be looked up in the wrong shard if sticky routing isn't enforced. We should check smart-router logs for that session id at the time range.

Maya (CSE): Matt — can you confirm whether the client sends a unique idempotency key in the initial POST (where they kick off the generation), or are you only relying on X-Client-Session/Resume-Id?

Matt (customer): we only use session/resume. Not an idempotency-key.

Jordan (eng-runtime): That's the crux. Best practice: include an idempotency key per logical generation attempt. Resume is for stream continuation; idempotency key prevents duplicate accepted work on server restarts/failovers. We'll triage whether the server should be stricter about deduping on session+resume.

Alice (eng-oncall): Short-term mitigation: ask client to attach Idempotency-Key header (UUID) on initial request. Server will check for existing completed generation and return the same completion id instead of starting new work. Long-term we need a fix in runtime to atomically claim a resume token on reconnect before scheduling new work.

Matt (customer): can you provide sample headers?

Maya (CSE): Send: `Idempotency-Key: uuid-v4` on initial POST and keep same Idempotency-Key if you retry. For SSE reconnects, still send Resume-Id but Idempotency-Key only needed for initial generation acceptance.

Jordan (eng-runtime): I'll open an internal ticket but need traces. Can you grant us the trace id from your second run? Look for header `X-Req-Trace` in their logs.

Matt (customer): trace id: trace-2026-06-11-88bfa. I pasted the full trace payload to support portal.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Received. Early look: router forwarded first connection to eu-west-2, second to eu-west-1. Sticky mapping failed due to ephemeral cache miss. eu-west-1 had no session kv entry so it created a new generation. That explains seq reset and duplicate charge.

Alice (eng-oncall): Action items: 1) eng-runtime: patch router to enforce session affinity or fallback to a read from global store before spinning new generation 2) platform: increase session KV TTL to reduce race windows 3) CSE: advise customer to add Idempotency-Key asap.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Agreed. I'll draft a hotfix to add an atomic claim step: when a resume token is presented, we attempt to lock session state (lease) in global store; if the lease isn't acquired, we return `event: resume_retry` instructing client to backoff and retry. That avoids simultaneous generation.

Maya (CSE): For product notes — could we add a `resume_status` event that tells clients whether resume succeeded vs start-fresh? Makes debugging easier.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Good idea. We can emit `event: resume_status` with `data: {status: "accepted"|"fresh", reason: "evicted"|"locked"|"no-token"}`. We'll be careful to not leak internal reasons to customers.

Matt (customer): If we can't change client immediately, is there a server-side toggle to disable creating new generation on resume mismatch? We want to avoid duplicate charges while we deploy client fix.

Alice (eng-oncall): We can add a temporary conservative mode per-tenant: if resume token is presented but session claim fails, return 409 to the client rather than start new generation. Ops needs tenant id to set flag. Maya, can you send tenant id to platform?

Maya (CSE): Sent tenant id over secure ticket.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Also logging improvements: log resume tokens and session shard hits in smart-router traces so we can easily see cross-region handoffs. I'll add that to the hotfix branch.

Maya (CSE): Matt — please try adding Idempotency-Key to initial request and confirm whether duplicates stop. Also try connecting twice to same region (force eu-west-2) as a short repro.

Matt (customer): Will do. Quick question: will adding Idempotency-Key double-charge if server already created a generation?

Jordan (eng-runtime): No — server will check for existing idempotency record and return the existing completion id/token usage; billing will be associated once. It prevents the second accept path from charging again.

Matt (customer): confirmed quick test: after adding Idempotency-Key duplicates stopped in 8/8 tries. Looks promising.

Alice (eng-oncall): Great. We'll keep working on router/session fixes and a per-tenant conservative toggle. Timelines: hotfix to router affinity + leasing by EOD for staging, rollout to prod early next week.

Maya (CSE): I'll update the ticket and advise customer (Matt) on next steps and timeline. Thanks everyone. :tada:
